title: Neural Puppet Theater
description: A ReadyPlayer.me avatar is connected to a BrainStem model via soft-body neural tendrils. The user manipulates energy nodes along the tendrils to control the avatar's limb movements, balancing neural energy conservation across the system. Undo/redo lets the user rewind puppet states while maintaining energy invariants.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a Neural Puppet Theater. Load BrainStem.glb and position it floating above-left as a pulsating brain controller. Load readyplayer.me.glb as a humanoid avatar standing center-right. Connect them with 6 soft-body catmull-rom spline tendrils rendered as glowing tubes from the brain to the avatar's head, shoulders, and hands. Each tendril has 2 draggable energy nodes (spheres) along its length that the user can click and drag to redistribute neural energy. The tendrils must simulate soft-body behavior using verlet integration with 12 mass points per tendril, responding to gravity and node manipulation with spring damping. Implement a global energy conservation law: total energy across all tendrils equals 100 units. When the user drags a node to increase energy on one tendril, other tendrils proportionally lose energy, visualized by tendril thickness and emissive color intensity from blue (low) to bright magenta (high). Energy level on each tendril drives corresponding avatar limb rotation via morph targets or bone manipulation: high energy means exaggerated movement, low means limp. Add a multi-input coupling mode activated by holding Shift while dragging, which locks two tendrils together so they share energy symmetrically. Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y that snapshots all node positions, energy distributions, and tendril states, supporting at least 14 history states. Use OrbitControls for camera with initial position at (0, 1.5, 4) looking at origin. Add hemisphere lighting (sky: 0x8888ff, ground: 0x443322) plus a point light near the brain with intensity modulated by total brain activity. Display a HUD overlay showing total system energy, per-tendril energy bars, and undo/redo step count. The interaction sequence involves: dragging 6 individual nodes, performing 2 shift-coupled drags, 2 undo operations, and 2 redo operations for 12 total steps.
